Convert a detset to glatos detections

Source: R/to_glatos.R
to_glatos.Rd

Returns the detections in the form glatos 0.9.8 reads: a data frame of class glatos_detections with the four columns its validator requires (animal_id, detection_timestamp_utc, deploy_lat, deploy_long) and the columns its filters and summaries use (transmitter_codespace, transmitter_id, receiver_sn, glatos_array, station_no, station, sensor_value, sensor_unit). glatos need not be installed.

Usage

to_glatos(x)

Arguments

x

A detset.

Value

A glatos_detections data frame, one row per detection, ordered as x$detections.

Details

glatos groups detections by glatos_array by default, as in glatos::detection_events(). Detections read from a GLATOS export keep their own glatos_array and station_no, so glatos groups them as it groups the export. Where a detection has none, as a lake array read from VUE or VDAT files does, glatos_array and station_no hold station_id; give location_col = "station" to glatos functions, or fill glatos_array with your own array codes. station holds station_id.

Positions come from the deployment that holds each detection under the half-open rule, or from the detection's own deploy_lat and deploy_lon where no deployment holds it. Raw sensor readings go to sensor_value with the unit "ADC", as GLATOS exports write them, where no calibrated value exists. Animal columns (common_name_e, tag_model, utc_release_date_time, release_latitude, release_longitude) come from the animals table. No row is removed.

Pass the result to glatos functions in memory. Written to a CSV, it is not a GLATOS export: glatos::read_glatos_detections() identifies a file by the full header of an export and stops on this one with "Detection file version could not be identified". Read such a CSV back with read_detset_from(), or with data.table::fread() and glatos::as_glatos_detections().

See also

read_detset_from() for the way back.

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
glatos_dets <- to_glatos(dets)
class(glatos_dets)
#> [1] "glatos_detections" "data.frame"       
head(glatos_dets[, c("animal_id", "detection_timestamp_utc", "transmitter_id",
           "receiver_sn")])
#>   animal_id detection_timestamp_utc transmitter_id receiver_sn
#> 1     ST-02     2024-06-02 15:50:39          61002        R012
#> 2     ST-02     2024-06-02 15:54:59          61002        R012
#> 3     ST-04     2024-06-02 15:56:56          61004        R009
#> 4     ST-02     2024-06-02 15:57:17          61002        R012
#> 5     ST-02     2024-06-02 15:59:22          61002        R012
#> 6     ST-04     2024-06-02 15:59:37          61004        R009
